titulo.texto: Recreation of a Shaft Tomb with Funerary Goods

frase_gancho.texto: A deep shaft and a chamber full of figures: this is how people were buried in the West.

puente_narrativo.texto: In the tombs there were companions and guardians. First, look for the dogs of red clay, round and shiny, with plump bodies and alert ears.

guion_corto.texto: You are standing before the reconstruction of a shaft tomb, the burial form typical of Jalisco, Nayarit and Colima about two thousand years ago. The idea is simple: a vertical shaft was dug, several meters deep, and at the bottom one or more chambers were opened. There the dead were laid, accompanied by clay figures, vessels with food, and jewelry. Unlike the Highlands, no great pyramids were raised here: the monumentality lay underground. Notice the contrast between the narrow, vertical shaft and the wide, vaulted chamber. And look at the figures all around: warriors, musicians, couples. It is an entire world buried to accompany the dead.

guion_largo.texto:
Compare three ways of thinking about death. In Palenque, King [Pakal](mna_s09_mascara_pakal) was buried inside a pyramid, at the foot of a staircase. In Monte Albán, in a stone chamber with paintings, like [Tomb 104](mna_s07_tumba_104). And here, in the West, in a shaft beneath the earth. Three regions, three architectures of death, and one shared wish: that the deceased have company and a good journey.

Some specialists see in the shape of these tombs, with their vertical shaft and round chamber, an image of the female body: the dead returned to the womb of the earth to be reborn. It is an interpretation, but it fits with other ideas you have already seen, such as the notion that to bury is to sow.

There is something even more surprising: the tombs were used many times. The shaft was opened again, the remains of the earlier dead were moved aside, and the newly deceased were laid to rest. The tomb was the home of a family across generations, not of a single person. That is why it is thought that in the chamber we do not see a single moment, but the accumulated memory of a lineage.

Alongside the dead, bowls were also left with seeds of corn, beans and squash, as well as jewelry made of sea shell. These were real offerings: it was believed that the dead needed to eat and to present themselves well in their new world. A tomb was, at once, a pantry, a jewelry box and a stage.

The most extraordinary thing about these tombs is what they contained. Thousands of clay figures, made to be buried, that show how people lived: warriors with helmets, musicians with conch-shell trumpets, couples, women carrying their children, healers, dogs, and even houses with their families inside, and banquets. Thanks to them we know the everyday life of the West better than that of many cultures with great pyramids.

Circular buildings have also been found. In Teuchitlán, Jalisco, a complex of round pyramids called Guachimontones was discovered, something very different from the square pyramids of the rest of the country. It is thought that some clay models from the West, with a small round plaza and figures who seem to be dancing, show precisely the rituals that took place there.

These tombs were looted for decades. The looters opened the shafts, took out the figures and sold them to collectors; that is why there are so many pieces from the West in museums around the world, but without our knowing which tomb they came from. A piece without context loses almost all of its story, and that is why this reconstruction is so valuable: it lets you imagine how the pieces were placed.

Some shafts reach sixteen meters in depth. Digging them with tools of stone and wood, in soft volcanic rock, was an enormous task. That was only done for someone very important.

When you look into the reconstruction, think about this: what you see is not above, but below. The true monument of the West is an emptiness beneath the earth, filled with people made of clay.

texto: Look at the vertical shaft and the side chamber: how are they connected?
Count how many different types of figures you can find among the grave goods
Compare the size of the shaft with your own height

texto.Culture: Shaft Tomb Tradition (associated with the Nayarit, Colima, and Jalisco cultures)
texto.Material: Museum recreation with human skeletons, clay vessels, hollow and solid figurines, stone grinding slabs, conch shells, and shell ornaments; the original chambers were carved into volcanic tuff, a soft volcanic rock
texto.Origin: Recreation based on archaeological contexts from Nayarit, Colima, and Jalisco

texto.pregunta: Myth: All the cultures of Mesoamerica buried their kings in pyramids.
texto.respuesta: Reality: In the West, people were buried in deep shafts with side chambers: their monumentality lay underground.
